attack: Strongest opposing claim is mean-reverter receive SOFR_2027-03: leftover +73bp of H7 hike premium after a >90% priced Sep hike, with the oil-supply tail reduced. They cite still-hot US gauges 72/75 and then fade anyway. That is fading aligned price, policy and revisions because the meeting was telegraphed.

No such print is in the packet. Receiving H7 toward 4.32 is a one-and-done assumption against a strip that still rises H7 4.58 / M7 4.72 / U7 4.755.

CFTC UST 2Y leveraged funds were already 93rd-percentile 1y short as of 15-Sep; that is crowded-trend risk, not evidence the hike extension was a squeeze that must reverse.

Higher overnight SOFR and a still-rising SR3 strip transmit that impulse into front-end yields. Housing-pain and ‘the hike was already priced’ are the transmission/fade narratives, not a reversal mechanism until inflation or labor actually breaks.

Futures entered that decision with >90% odds of 25bp. US 2Y then extended to 4.76 (+8.999999999999986bp 1d, +56.99999999999994bp 1m, +125.0bp 1y). SR3 strip as of the frozen packet: SR3U6 4.0, SR3Z6 4.32, SR3H7 4.58, SR3M7 4.72, SR3U7 4.755 then a gentle decline. Parallel AU/CA front-end yields also rose over 1m (AU 2Y +39.1bp to 4.999; CA 2Y +31.0bp to 3.27) but the 1d impulse was US-up (AU 2Y −5.5bp that day).
context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known: August CPI had already kept a Fed tightening bias, and the 25bp hike was >90% priced into 16 September. New enough to trade now: the hike was delivered, SOFR gap-up to 3.85, US 2Y kept rising into 18 September rather than ‘selling the fact’, and the last-24h desk thesis plus BoJ 1.25% hike/BoE 6–3 split show the global easing impulse remaining constrained. AU housing (NSW stamp duty −24% y/y, volumes −18%, Sydney/Melbourne values >7% off peak) is known tightening-channel news, not a US reversal print.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: The SOFR path treats the cycle as largely a two-to-three-hike affair from 3.85 cash toward a 2027 peak near 4.755 (SR3U7) then slight easing (SR3H8 4.695). That assumes labor/inflation cool enough to cap terminal rates below 5% even though US 5Y is already 4.86 and US 10Y 5.01.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: The priced assumption that is wrong is that the delivered, well-telegraphed 25bp hike and 99th-percentile yield levels are a peak to fade. Trend persistence says the hiking/higher-yield regime continues and the SR3 2027 peak is too low, not that mean-reversion starts because the move is ‘done’ or because housing is hurting.
